archetype.name: Rebuilding (defense-first problem)
archetype.definition: A team in its second straight season near the bottom of the league, whose results turn on whether a historically leaky defense can be fixed, not on the standings.

report.headline: Same 121.5 defense as last year's 22-win team, and now no Sabonis
report.take:
Sacramento is 1-9, 29th on the site, with a Net Rtg of -13.2 that ranks 27th. This is not a new slump. Last season ended 22-60 with a defensive rating of 121.5, and the defensive rating this year is exactly 121.5 again, 28th in the league. The offense has stayed in the same bottom tier too, 26th by offensive rating both seasons. Ten games is a small sample, but it matches the 82 before it almost number for number. That makes this a continuation, not an early-season fluke.

The defense is the story, and it is an odd one. The Kings keep opponents away from the basket better than most: Opp Rim Rate of 26.2 ranks 6th, and they finish possessions on the glass with a DRB % that ranks 8th. When teams do get to the rim, though, they convert 75% of the time. That is last in the league and nearly ten points above the league average. Opponents also hit 37.9% from three, the same mark as last season, so the overall Opp eFG % of 57.9 sits 29th. Opposing centers and power forwards take a bigger share of the scoring against Sacramento than the league norm, which points to the interior. The offense adds little cover. Darius Acuff Jr. carries a 32.3 USG % on 51.8 TS %, the team rarely gets to the line (FT Rate 23rd), and turnovers run high (TOV % 24th). Zach LaVine's 63.2 TS % is the most efficient volume scoring on the roster.

The record is not hiding bad luck. W vs Pt Diff is -1, and the margin implies just 2 wins, so 1-9 is roughly what the play earned. What the full-season line does hide is the gap between October and November. October was 0-6 with 128.33 points allowed a game. November has been 1-3 with 113.5 allowed. The last five games allowed 4.4 fewer points a game than the season average. Some of that is real tightening, and some is October's blowouts dragging the average. The on-off numbers are mostly ten-game noise: LaVine at -23.9, Emanuel Sharp at +25.6, and Domantas Sabonis at -7.2 despite a 71.6 TS % and the roster's best BPM. Sabonis, 10th on his position's tab, is now listed Out. That strips the frontcourt's one above-average player from a group already graded D+.

The current pace says 8 wins, which is too low for a team showing November's defensive form. Still, nothing here points to the middle of the West. Expect a bottom-five finish unless the rim numbers fall back toward last year's level, which was poor but not historic.

strengths.title: Limits rim attempts, cleans the glass
strengths.body: Opponents take only 26.2% of their shots at the rim, 6th-fewest in the league. The Kings also grab their opponents' misses at a rate that ranks 8th. That is a sound shell for a defense: it keeps possessions to one shot and pushes opponents to the perimeter. It should hold, since rim rate and defensive rebounding are more stable than make rates. The open question is whether it survives Sabonis's absence.

strengths.title: LaVine's efficient volume scoring
strengths.body: LaVine is scoring at a 63.2 TS % on a 25.4 USG %, the one efficient high-usage option on a 26th-ranked offense. The -23.9 On-Off is a ten-game lineup artifact more than a verdict. A shooter with that efficiency is the offense's best tool while Sabonis is out.

strengths.title: Leaky Black's minutes work
strengths.body: In 115 minutes, Black has a 4.9 BPM and a 67.6 TS %, and he ranks 21st on the small-forward tab. He is the only wing who ranks in the top half, on a wing group graded F. The sample is tiny and his usage is low, but he has earned a longer look.

concerns.title: Worst rim defense in the league
concerns.body: Opponents finish 75% of their attempts within four feet, last in the league and 9.8 points above the league average. Opposing centers and power forwards take a bigger share of the points than the league norm. Some regression is likely, since last season's 69.8 was bad but not this bad. Without Sabonis, though, there is no obvious source of improvement.

concerns.title: Sabonis out, frontcourt thin
concerns.body: Sabonis has been the team's best player: 10th on his position's tab, a 71.6 TS %, a 3.3 BPM and the most Win Shares on the roster. Behind him are Precious Achiuwa at a -1.5 BPM, Keegan Murray and Jonathan Mogbo in limited minutes with poor efficiency, and Dylan Cardwell in just 47 minutes. The D+ frontcourt grade was earned with Sabonis in it, so expect it to get worse while he is out.

concerns.title: Inefficient offense, high-usage guard
concerns.body: Acuff uses 32.3% of possessions on a 51.8 TS %. The team does not create extra chances: ORB % ranks 26th, FT Rate 23rd and TOV % 24th. The offensive rating of 108.3 trails the league by 5.1. That is a structural problem, not a shooting slump.

trend.note: October's 0-6 came with 128.33 points allowed a game, and November's 1-3 has allowed 113.5, a real defensive tightening. The last five games are still 1-4 with a -10 margin, though, and Sabonis has just gone out.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games: Orlando is the chance, then two contenders
weekAhead.body:
All three games are in Sacramento, but the opposition gets much stronger after the opener. Orlando (2-7, 24th on the site) is the one comparable team: 27th in offensive rating, 26th in defensive rating, and as weak as the Kings at the rim. That game on the 10th is the clear opportunity. Portland (6-3, 3rd on the site) has already won in Sacramento 128-120 and brings the 3rd-best offense. Oklahoma City (8-2) has the league's best defense.

The realistic target is one win, against Orlando. Against Portland and OKC, the measure is whether November's improved defense holds without Sabonis. Portland's A- frontcourt and free-throw volume aim straight at the Kings' weakest spot. OKC's rim protection will smother whatever interior offense is left.

keyMatchups.title: Orlando: two bottom-tier offenses
keyMatchups.body: Orlando's offensive rating of 107.9 is even worse than Sacramento's, and the Magic take 47% of their shots from three. That is a threat, since the Kings allow 37.9% from deep. Orlando gives up 28.78 points a game to power forwards, 29th in the league, so there is an opening for the Kings' forwards to attack.

keyMatchups.title: Portland's frontcourt against a soft rim
keyMatchups.body: Portland has an A- frontcourt and the league's 2nd-highest FT Rate, and it has already scored 128 in Sacramento this season. The Blazers also allow the most points to opposing centers in the league. That puts pressure on Achiuwa to punish them with Sabonis out.

keyMatchups.title: OKC's elite rim defense
keyMatchups.body: Oklahoma City's defensive rating of 105.5 and Opp Rim FG % of 55.5 both lead the league. The Thunder have held centers furthest below their usual scoring of any team. Their soft spot is shooting guards, who score 28.7 points a game against them (23rd), so this game probably runs through LaVine.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the points allowed stay near November's 113.5 a game now that Sabonis is out, starting against Orlando on the 10th.

restOfSeason.body:
The 8-win pace is too pessimistic. October's blowouts weigh heavily on a 10-game average, and a rim FG % of 75 is extreme enough that some regression toward last year's poor-but-normal levels is likely. Even so, the profile is last season's 22-60 team almost exactly: the same defensive rating, the same offensive rank and the same 37.9% allowed from three. The lack of a pythDiff cushion means there is no hidden bad luck to give back. Expect something in the range of 15 to 22 wins, with a net rating that improves toward -9 but stays bottom-five.

What holds up: the defensive rebounding and the low rate of rim attempts allowed, plus LaVine's efficiency. What should regress: the 75% at the rim and some of the extreme on-off splits. What decides whether they climb toward the top of that range is how long Sabonis is out. He is the only above-average frontcourt player on the roster.

confidence.note: Only 10 games, but they closely mirror last season's 82.
